name: OpenFOAM (OpenFOAM Foundation / CFD Direct; OpenCFD Ltd under ESI Group and Keysight)
origin_detail: FOAM was developed in C++ by Henry Weller and Hrvoje Jasak (roots in David Gosman's group at Imperial College London; the early-1990s date is uncited on Wikipedia) and sold commercially by Nabla Ltd. After Nabla folded, Weller, Chris Greenshields and Mattijs Janssens founded OpenCFD Ltd, which released the code under the GPL as OpenFOAM on 10 Dec 2004. Copyright moved to the OpenFOAM Foundation in 2011 (England, company limited by guarantee since 2014); OpenCFD kept the trademark and passed to SGI (2011), ESI Group (2012) and, via Keysight's 2023 control of ESI, to Keysight.
openness_notes: FOAM was a commercial product (Nabla Ltd) before the 2004 GPL release. Today both main lines are GPL; the openfoam.org line's copyright is held by the non-profit OpenFOAM Foundation Ltd (scored 4), while the openfoam.com line is developed by OpenCFD (Keysight/ESI) with a 2018 governance steering committee including Volkswagen, General Motors and FM Global (closer to 3). The name 'OpenFOAM' is an OpenCFD trademark (since 2007).

license_history.note: Released 10 Dec 2004; earlier FOAM was proprietary

license_history.license: GPL; copyright transferred to OpenFOAM Foundation
license_history.note: 5 Aug 2011 to OpenFOAM Foundation Inc. (Delaware); re-incorporated in England 25 Apr 2014

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Became the leading open-source CFD toolkit; later split into openfoam.org (CFD Direct, from 2015) and openfoam.com (OpenCFD, date-versioned from 2016) lines plus foam-extend.

exit_events.note: SGI acquired OpenCFD on 8 Aug 2011, days after copyright moved to the Foundation
ESI acquired OpenCFD (and the OpenFOAM trademark) from SGI, announced 12 Sep 2012
Keysight completed purchase of a 50.6% controlling block of ESI Group at EUR 155 per share on 3 Nov 2023, bringing OpenCFD under Keysight; total value not stated in release

risk_events: 2015-2016 split: Weller and Greenshields left OpenCFD to form CFD Direct (Mar 2015); two parallel 'OpenFOAM' release lines plus foam-extend now coexist.
Copyright (Foundation) and trademark (OpenCFD, now Keysight-controlled) are held by different parties.
Nov 2025: the Foundation called its EUR 250k/yr maintenance funding 'inadequate' and set a 2026 target of EUR 500k; CFD Direct, which maintains openfoam.org, is 'a company of 5 people'.
Sep 2024: ESI's CEO resigned as a director of OpenFOAM Foundation Ltd.
robustness: Code is GPL and has been forked repeatedly, so it cannot be closed; but each main line depends on a small team (CFD Direct: 5 people) funded by maintenance plans (EUR 5,000 / 25,000 / 100,000 per year tiers). The corporate parent of OpenCFD changed three times (SGI, ESI, Keysight) without the code disappearing.
physical_science_relevance: The leading open-source CFD code, used across academic fluid mechanics, combustion, multiphase flow and industrial engineering; the main open alternative to Ansys Fluent and other commercial CFD.
openness_effect_assessment: Opening FOAM in 2004 gave it a user base the Foundation says broadly matches major proprietary CFD packages 'despite having only a small fraction of their resources'. Openness also made it acquirable piecemeal (SGI, ESI, Keysight bought the company and trademark, not the code) and led to fragmentation into competing lines, while maintenance remains chronically underfunded.
key_takeaway: OpenFOAM is the open CFD comparator to Ansys: comparable reach, but its maintainers run on about EUR 250k a year while Ansys sold for $35B. GPL licensing protected the code through three changes of corporate owner and a developer split, but did not solve sustainability; the Foundation's own 2025 appeal says funding must double.
